text:
alex: quick follow-up from the softshrink RFC — exploring a 'reservation then shrink' flow to reduce fragmentation without starving live inference. thoughts?

rachel: curious, can you sketch the happy path? hard to picture interplay with async offload.

alex: idea: when an allocation is created we optionally attach a small reservation token (eg 1-4 pages) that guarantees quick re-reserve during transient spikes. if memory pressure persists > grace window we shrink to 0 and mark block reclaimable.

diego: so reservation is per-allocation, not per-tenant? how do we avoid token explosion for tiny allocs?
alex: per-allocation but sampled. we only issue tokens for allocations > threshold (eg >128KB) and up to a cap per-heap. heuristics can be workload-driven.

matt: what's the grace window? fixed or adaptive?
alex: adaptive preferred — e.g. base 200ms, backoff multiply with recent eviction churn. want short for low-latency paths, longer for batched workloads.

rachel: how does this interact with KV-cache and prefix caching? must avoid reloading model KV if we keep shrinking.
diego: right. maybe we bias tokens toward allocations that touch KV cache or pinned embeddings. we already track hotness; token grant could consult hot-score.

alex: exactly. grant_token = hot_score > H and allocation_size > S and tenant_quota > 0. if grant fails fallback to immediate shrink.

matt: concerns: token accounting across nodes + crash cases. if a node dies we need fast reclamation.

alex: infra-bot can help — we can piggyback on existing lease heartbeats. token TTL = 1s; renew every 200ms. on heartbeat loss token auto-expire.

infra-bot: reminder: lease/heartbeat infra already emits events to /events/lease for dead nodes. integrating token TTL shouldn't need new RPCs; just reuse existing liveness checks. :white_check_mark:

rachel: oom mitigation: what are fallback policies? do we prefer model variant fallback or immediate eviction of softshrunk blocks?
alex: policy stack: 1) try local reclaim of softshrunk reclaimable blocks; 2) escalate to eviction of low-hotness allocations; 3) route requests to cheaper variant (quantized) as last resort. tunable per-route.
diego: and preemption? high-priority requests should steal reservations? racey but necessary.
alex: allow priority override: allocators expose a try_steal(token_id) API that atomically transfers token if current holder not in critical section. callers must be careful.
matt: API semantics need to be simple. maybe: `reserve(token_key, priority)` returns token or null. `steal(token_key)` returns boolean with audit log. add counters for debugging.

rachel: telemetry wishlist: token grants, steals, TTL expirations, evictor steps. without these it will be impossible to debug regressions.
alex: agreed — will add metrics: token_grants{tenant,route}, token_steals, token_expirations, reclaim_latency_histogram. also trace spans for reservation lifecycle.

diego: performance: stamping tokens into allocation header adds a few bytes — ok. but we must avoid cacheline blowups on hot paths. pack into 8 bytes and avoid false sharing.
alex: implementation note: use atomic 64-bit word in allocation metadata: lower bits for token id, upper bits for flags/timestamp. cheap to read.

matt: tests: stress harness with bursty inference + induced node death, verify no leaks and bounded re-reserve latency. also replay of production traces for percentiles.
alex: plan: prototype in feature branch, lightweight opt-in via config flags per-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private). will start a PoC this week.
rachel: sounds good. one more: can we make softshrink advisory so model loaders can pin critical segments? some frameworks need explicit pin calls.
alex: yes — add `pin()` semantics that bypass reservation shrink and mark as persistent until explicit `unpin()`. pin can be rate-limited and audited.
diego: ok i'm +1 for prototype. happy to help on hot-score integration.
matt: same, i'll wire tests and API guards.

alex: thanks all — I'll open the branch with a short design doc and a smoke test matrix. ping me if you want to be on the PR reviewers list. :rocket:
